headline: Drupal and GeoServer join KEV as a 9.8 Linux root bug surfaces
standfirst: CISA confirmed active exploitation of three vulnerabilities — two in GeoServer and a 9.8-rated Drupal Core flaw — while Drupal's own team warned of a second critical bug already being used to hijack sites. Switzerland disclosed AI-agent intrusions at critical infrastructure operators, and the vulnerability queue filled with a 12-year-old Linux NFS root flaw and an unpatched Cacti RCE that already has public exploit code. Add a reported Air Force cloud breach, a confirmed SAP incident and trojanized installers, and the patch list is long.
bodyMarkdown:
## Actively exploited

CISA added three entries to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on evidence of active exploitation: an XML injection flaw in GeoServer (CVE-2026-120705), an incorrect authorization flaw in the same product (CVE-2026-129243), and an improper check for unusual or exceptional conditions in Drupal Core (CVE-2026-136716) [[s11]]. Only the Drupal entry carries NVD enrichment, and it is severe: CVSS 9.8, critical, with a network vector that requires no privileges and no user interaction, tracked as CWE-754, affecting Drupal core before 10.6.23 and the 11.x lines before 11.3.23 and 11.4.14. The two GeoServer records supply vendor, product and name but no severity or affected versions. CISA's required action points to vendor mitigations under BOD 26-04, with a remediation deadline falling only days after listing — a federal requirement, not a universal one. Ransomware campaign use is recorded as unknown for all three. Analysis: the unenriched GeoServer entries are the awkward ones, since severity-based triage is impossible from the catalog alone and patch guidance has to come from the vendor.

Drupal's security team says attackers are exploiting a second critical vulnerability that lets them breach and hijack unpatched websites [[s16]]. The supplied reporting gives no CVE, no affected versions and no exploitation mechanism, so it should not be merged with the KEV entry above until that link is confirmed. The practical consequence is that exposure here is framed as full site takeover rather than defacement.

## Vulnerabilities

A 12-year-old flaw in the Linux kernel's NFS server, CVE-2026-99362, allows remote attackers to gain root privileges and is rated 9.8 critical on a network vector with no privileges or user interaction required [[s21]]. The supplied description describes nfsd narrowing a reply buffer to the session's cached limit before accepting the slot seqid; a COMPOUND tag can then fill that buffer without the status word, leaving the operation marked successful and copying the reply into a zero-length slot buffer — a slab-out-of-bounds write. The NVD record lists no affected configurations, so kernel version auditing has to start from distribution advisories rather than from the advisory data itself. The CVE is a confirmed KEV miss, which does not establish that exploitation has not occurred.

Cacti has a publicly disclosed zero-day with a proof-of-concept exploit that lets unauthenticated attackers execute commands on vulnerable monitoring servers [[s3]]. No CVE has been assigned in the supplied reporting and no patch is described, which leaves the usual choice between exposure reduction and waiting.

## Breaches

Hackers have reportedly breached the Air Force's Cloud One computing platform, described as part of a wave of attacks reportedly affecting other federal agencies [[s6]]. Everything here is reported rather than confirmed, and the supplied text gives no detail on access method or data touched — treat attribution and scope as open.

SAP confirmed a cybersecurity incident following reports that intruders reached its software development infrastructure and may have accessed source code [[s10]]. The confirmation covers the incident; the source-code access is still reported. Analysis: if code was in fact taken, the concern shifts from SAP's own perimeter to the trust its enterprise customers place in shipped software — but the supplied evidence does not establish that theft occurred.

Switzerland's cybersecurity agency said attackers using AI agents broke into systems in four of five confirmed attacks, the country's first such cases [[s24]]. Three targeted critical infrastructure operators, two of those succeeded, and no major disruptions were reported. Victims were not named and the perpetrator is not known, so the AI-agent element is the agency's characterization of the attacks, not an identified actor.

## Research

Installers for Q-Dir and DesktopOK distributed through the official SoftwareOK site were tampered with to deliver remote access malware, with evidence that malicious files were generated both on direct download from the official page and during the update process of already-installed copies [[s19]]. The update-channel path is the part worth noting: users who did nothing unusual beyond accepting an update were still in scope.

selected.excerpt: CISA has added three new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog, based on evidence of active exploitation. CVE-2026-120705 OSGeo GeoServer XML Injection Vulnerability CVE-2026-129243 OSGeo GeoServer Incorrect Authorization Vulnerability CVE-2026-136716 Drupal Core Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions Vulnerability These types of vulnerabilities are a…

kev.shortDescription: OsGeo GeoServer contains an XML injection vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to cause the server to read local text files accessible to the GeoServer process or fetch attacker-specified HTTP or HTTPS URLs via a crafted ID parameter in the WFS 2.0 GetFeatureById stored query. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-129244, CVE-2026-129243, CVE-2026-129245, and CVE-2026-129242 to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution on an affected GeoServer instance.
kev.requiredAction: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.

kev.shortDescription: GeoServer contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to bypass service-level role checks and invoke operations protected solely by those checks via a request with a prefixed service parameter. This vulnerability can be chained with CVE-2026-129244, CVE-2026-120705, CVE-2026-129245, and CVE-2026-129242 to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution on an affected GeoServer instance.

selected.title: New NFS2ROOT Linux flaw can let attackers gain root privileges
selected.excerpt: ​A 12-year-old critical vulnerability in the Linux kernel's Network File System (NFS) server, tracked as CVE-2026-99362, allows remote attackers to gain root privileges. [...]

nvd.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

nfsd: preflight SEQUENCE replies before accepting a slot

nfsd4_sequence() narrows the reply buffer to the session's cached
reply limit before it accepts the slot seqid. A client may negotiate
ca_maxresponsesize_cached down to NFSD_MIN_HDR_SEQ_SZ, and
nfsd4_alloc_slot() then gives every slot a zero-length sl_data[]. A
COMPOUND tag can fill that narrowed buffer until it holds the
SEQUENCE opcode but not the status word that follows.
nfsd4_encode_operation() returns without running
nfsd4_encode_sequence(), so cstate.data_offset stays zero. It leaves
op->status at nfs_ok as well, so the COMPOUND is treated as having
succeeded.

nfsd4_store_cache_entry() declines to cache a lone SEQUENCE that
returned an error. That test reads the status the operation
reported, so it passes here. The copy starts at offset zero and
takes the whole reply, RPC and COMPOUND headers included, into the
zero-length sl_data[]. The COMPOUND tag is copied along with it, so
the client picks most of the bytes written past the end of the slot:

  BUG: KASAN: slab-out-of-bounds in read_bytes_from_xdr_buf+0x1bc/0x390
  Write of size 80 at addr ffff888003a549cd by task kunit_try_catch/24
   __asan_memcpy+0x38/0x60
   read_bytes_from_xdr_buf+0x1bc/0x390
   nfsd4_sequence_done+0x5b0/0x810
   nfs4svc_encode_compoundres+0x1bf/0x240

Check that the fixed-size SEQUENCE result, plus room for a following
operation's error status, fits the negotiated limit before narrowing
the buffer and consuming the slot seqid. The slot and its reply
cache are left unchanged, as RFC 8881 Section 2.10.6.1.2 requires of
an error returned from SEQUENCE.
